heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation creative output with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — advanced ByteDance models built for premium image generation, cinematic video, and precise multimodal control.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a bold brand-orange hero with a dark cinematic overlay and a layered product-console composition rather than a simple split. Place the headline inside a left-aligned copy block over the orange field, while the right side carries a stacked media collage: one large preview frame for Seedance, one grid of Seedream outputs, and a slim floating UI shell to imply professional workflow. Add subtle grid lines, soft orbs, and gradient mesh accents for depth. Keep the CTA in Techjockey orange with strong contrast, and make the hero feel premium, enterprise-ready, and proof-led.

repetitionBreakers: Hero uses a split, orange-led launch composition with cinematic product visuals; the next section switches to a dark, compact trust/proof band.
How-it-works is rendered as a three-step horizontal process, then proof shifts to a static logo grid instead of another text block.
Feature sections alternate between an interactive tabs-with-preview product block and a visual-first split panel to avoid repeating the same layout rhythm.
Testimonials use a spotlight carousel after dense product content, then pricing closes with clean highlighted cards before the final CTA.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate premium AI images and videos with ByteDance models Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore the 3-step workflow, trusted logos, standout features, pricing, and request a demo with Get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: solid brand-orange field with dark layered media shell and subtle dashboard-grid texture
sections.designNote: Make the headline answer what this is immediately: AI image and video generation for professional visual teams. Keep the subheadline explicit about who it is for: creative directors, video producers, art directors, marketing managers, and creative leads. Use the CTA label only as Get started in a solid accent button at 100% opacity. The right side should feel like a premium model-output workspace with image tiles, video frames, and prompt-to-result previews. This must be visually dominant and feel like continuity from the ad.

Place trust immediately after the hero because traffic is warm and the proof strategy is logos-first. Use 3-6 recognizable customer or partner logos if available; if not, convert this into a clean metrics strip. Keep it compact, dark, and highly credible so it reads like enterprise validation rather than decoration.

Introduce a 3-step process that can be understood in under 60 seconds: 1) enter prompt or source media, 2) choose image or video generation path, 3) review and export results. Keep copy concise and action-oriented. Use a lighter, breathable section after the dark trust band so the page rhythm opens up and stays easy to scan on mobile.

If recognizable logos are present, this should remain a logo grid; otherwise use a tight metric strip. Since the supplied trust data is weak, reinforce proof with concise credibility markers such as enterprise-ready infrastructure, multimodal content creation, and fast inference. Keep this section lean and non-generic.

Start with Seedream 4.5 because it is the most click-relevant image-generation product. Use tabs-with-preview for the five features so the user can scan advanced text-image alignment, high-resolution output, typographic rendering, multi-image composition, and structural fidelity without a flat grid. The preview panel should show before/after visual refinement. This section should feel premium and hands-on.

Make this section visually distinct from the image block by flipping to a dark, cinematic split panel. Focus on the video product: text-to-video generation, audio-visual synchronization, multilingual lip-sync, cinematic camera control, and 10x faster inference. Use a compact mock video gallery or stacked thumbnail rail on the visual side to reinforce motion and sound together. This should feel like a dedicated reveal, not an afterthought.

Use a carousel or spotlight treatment because there are 5 testimonials. Keep the quote cards premium and role-led, highlighting creative director, video producer, art director, marketing manager, and creative lead voices. This section should lean into confidence and workflow impact, not generic praise.

Present pricing as two clean highlighted cards rather than a dense comparison table. Emphasize the image and video products separately, and keep the CTA button copy consistent as Get started. The video plan can carry the starting price detail while the image plan emphasizes quote-based enterprise evaluation.

Close with a high-contrast lead form or final CTA panel that feels like the conversion endpoint. Keep the field set minimal and the CTA button solid accent orange at full opacity, labeled Get started. On mobile, the CTA must be full-width. The supporting copy should reinforce seeing the product in action rather than signing up generically.
Use this only if there are additional recognizable media or partner logos. Do not animate as a marquee. If no strong logos are available, omit this section entirely rather than forcing weak proof.

blueprint.designPersonality: A premium enterprise AI studio for visual creation: structured, cinematic, proof-heavy, and brand-forward. The layout should feel intelligent and highly usable for creative professionals, with Techjockey trust signals and partner logos taking center stage, strong section contrast, and a dedicated video gallery to make Seedance feel vivid and concrete.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use premium AI-generated style visuals, mock video frames, model output grids, prompt-to-result sequences, and floating UI shells. The hero should show a cinematic content workspace with image tiles, timeline strips, and output previews. The video gallery section should present stacked thumbnail cards with play affordances, motion blur hints, and frame counters. Keep visuals dark, polished, and enterprise-ready rather than playful or consumer-facing.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and product-specific, so 40px keeps it readable without wrapping awkwardly on the hero.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette is locked to Techjockey’s provided colors, so the page should use #ff6b00 as the hero background and primary CTA color, with white, charcoal, and light gray for supporting surfaces. referenceMap.heroPattern: Split-impact hero with brand/logo placement, large centered headline, short supporting copy, and a compact bullet-value list beneath. Strong left-to-right hierarchy, minimal CTAs in the hero, and a high-contrast visual band that separates the opener from the rest of the page.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-page sales flow with a prominent hero followed by a lead-capture form, then stacked product/feature sections. Sections are separated by clear vertical spacing and alternating emphasis rather than dense multi-column content.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Utility-first content blocks with simple rectangular containers, light borders or subtle shadows, and highly legible text. Cards prioritize scannability over decoration and use short titled feature items in a list-like format.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion happens through a single dominant CTA in the hero and a form submission CTA lower on the page. Secondary actions are minimal or absent, reinforcing a focused lead-generation path.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing-first pattern in the reference structure. If pricing is present in the source system, it should be introduced as a separate conversion section with plan cards, but the observed layout does not emphasize comparison tables or tiers in the main viewport.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in the provided reference markup. Likely a standard utility footer rather than a marketing-heavy closing section.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Primarily text-led with logo/header imagery and no prominent product media. The page favors structural hierarchy and form capture over large illustrative or video-led panels.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Modular feature sections with a label tag, headline, descriptive paragraph, and a list of 4-5 feature points. Each section is self-contained and optimized for quick scanning, with optional CTA placement at the section level.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead form embedded immediately after the hero, presented in a card-like container with a strong heading. Includes hidden tracking fields, indicating CRM/attribution integration and a conversion-oriented submission flow.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, conversion-focused presentation with no evidence of motion-led storytelling. Interaction is likely limited to standard form behavior and basic responsive adjustments.
designNotes: Use a strong first-screen hierarchy with headline, brief value statement, and 3 supporting benefits.
Keep CTAs singular and decisive to reduce choice friction.
Place lead capture early, directly after the hero, for high-intent traffic.
Prefer simple, scannable feature lists over dense paragraphs.
Use dark or high-contrast hero treatment to create a clear opening band.
Maintain generous whitespace and straightforward grid alignment.
Avoid reliance on interactive gimmicks; the layout should read as enterprise B2B and form-driven.

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should behave like a premium, solution-aware lead-generation landing page for two tightly related AI generative products. The audience is professional and quality-sensitive, so the design should feel futuristic, credible, and product-led rather than playful or consumer-oriented. Because the visitor trusts logos most, trust needs to be introduced early as a logo-first strip or brand rail, supported by testimonials later. The hero should stay message-led and compact, with a split layout that balances strong copy and product visualization without relying on a form. A dark theme with high-contrast AI media will suit the subject matter and help the video gallery section stand out. The flow should remain balanced: hero, trust, product feature blocks, video gallery, pricing/quote, testimonials, and final CTA.
